Settings reference

Source: vignettes/settings.Rmd
settings.Rmd

This page lists every setting in harnessr, stage by stage, and the building blocks those settings choose between. harnessr builds the tables from gr_settings_table() and the registries when the page is built, so they match the installed code.

A setting with a walkthrough links to it. The walkthrough is a section of a guide that covers what the setting trades off, the signs that you should change it, where its default came from and how to test a change.

library(harnessr)
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
settings <- gr_settings_table()
table(settings$stage, settings$tier)[unique(settings$stage), ]
#>             
#>              advanced basic
#>   ingest           18     3
#>   segment          17     3
#>   read             42     8
#>   screen           22    11
#>   extract           7     3
#>   synthesise       24     5
#>   evaluate         20    10
#>   options          29     5

Reading the tables

Each row is one setting, and these columns describe it:

  • where: the function that takes the setting.
  • default: the value used when you give none. A string appears without quotes, a set of choices shows its first choice, and anything else appears as R code.
  • tier: basic for the few settings most runs change, advanced for the rest.
  • status: where the default came from. measured means a measurement backs it, cited means a published source gives it, and untested means it was chosen and nothing has measured it. A blank means nothing is declared, as for switches, limits and most function arguments.

gr_settings_table() also returns the source behind each status. For the full help, see ?gr_read_spec, ?gr_segment_spec, ?gr_ingest_spec and ?hr_options.

You give a setting where its stage takes it. Ingest, segment and read settings go in a spec (gr_read_spec(top_k = 4)), in a recipe, or by name to answer_document(), gr_read_many() and gr_arm(), which put each on the step it belongs to. Review and evaluation settings are arguments of their functions. You set options for the session with hr_options().

To find out whether a value works better on your documents, build one arm per value with hr_sweep() and compare the arms with hr_benchmark() and hr_report(), as vignette("compare") does. hr_sweep_check() reports which values sent the same requests.

show_settings <- function(stage) {
  s <- settings[settings$stage == stage, ]
  esc <- function(x) gsub("|", "\\|", ifelse(is.na(x), "", x), fixed = TRUE)
  name <- ifelse(is.na(s$guide), paste0("`", s$name, "`"),
                 sprintf("[`%s`](%s.html#%s)", s$name, sub("#.*", "", s$guide),
                         sub(".*#", "", s$guide)))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = name, where = paste0("`", s$where, "`"),
                          default = paste0("`", esc(s$default), "`"),
                          tier = s$tier, status = esc(s$status),
                          description = esc(s$description)),
               row.names = FALSE)
}

Ingest

These settings control what comes out of a file: cleaning, OCR, the PDF layout pass, and the floor on how much text must survive. The entries of cleaner_opts and layout_opts appear under their parent’s name, as cleaner_opts.references_after. vignette("ingest") covers them.

setting where default tier status description
ocr gr_ingest_spec() auto basic untested When to OCR a page: with no text layer, always, or never.
layout gr_ingest_spec() auto advanced untested How a PDF page’s text is put in reading order.
clean gr_ingest_spec() standard basic untested A cleaning preset, or cleaner names.
ocr_lang gr_ingest_spec() eng advanced untested Tesseract language code.
ocr_dpi gr_ingest_spec() 300 advanced cited Render density for PDF OCR.
ocr_min_chars gr_ingest_spec() 40 advanced untested A page with fewer characters is OCRed under ocr = ‘auto’.
min_chars gr_ingest_spec() 20 basic untested Refuse the document if less text than this survives.
extractor gr_ingest_spec() NULL advanced untested Force an extractor instead of choosing by file type.
parallel gr_ingest_spec() NULL advanced untested Parallelise page-level OCR.
cleaner_opts gr_ingest_spec() list() advanced untested Extra options passed to individual cleaners.
layout_opts gr_ingest_spec() list() advanced untested Settings of the PDF running-head pass under layout = ‘auto’.
ocr_trigger gr_ingest_spec() raw_text advanced untested Which text of a PDF page ocr_min_chars is counted on under ocr = ‘auto’.
ocr_confidence gr_ingest_spec() FALSE advanced untested Record Tesseract’s confidence on a PDF page’s OCR blocks (a second pass).
cleaner_opts.references_after gr_ingest_spec() 0.4 advanced untested For the references cleaner: the share of the text after which a References heading ends the text.
cleaner_opts.header_max_chars gr_ingest_spec() 80 advanced untested For the headers_footers cleaner: the longest line that can be taken for a running head or foot.
cleaner_opts.header_min_repeats gr_ingest_spec() 3 advanced untested For headers_footers: how many times a line must recur to be taken for a running head; values below 3 are read as 3.
layout_opts.depth gr_ingest_spec() 2 advanced untested Lines at each edge of a PDF page that are candidates for a running head or foot.
layout_opts.share gr_ingest_spec() 0.4 advanced untested The share of pages a line must recur on to be dropped as a running head or foot.
layout_opts.min_pages gr_ingest_spec() 3 advanced untested The fewest pages a document needs before any line is dropped, and the fewest a line must recur on.
layout_opts.max_chars gr_ingest_spec() 200 advanced untested The longest line, in characters, that can be a running head or foot.
layout_opts.max_words gr_ingest_spec() 5 advanced untested Above this many words, a numbered line must carry its number where a page number is set.

Segment

harnessr cuts the text into chunks with these settings. vignette("segment") covers them.

setting where default tier status description
context_source gr_segment_spec() metadata advanced untested For contextual: where the context line comes from.
max_tokens gr_segment_spec() 1200 basic untested Hard cap on chunk size, in tokens.
overlap_tokens gr_segment_spec() 0 basic untested Tokens of trailing context copied into the start of the next chunk.
min_tokens gr_segment_spec() 0 advanced untested A smaller chunk is merged into the one before it.
method gr_segment_spec() paragraph basic untested The segmentation strategy.
separators gr_segment_spec() NULL advanced untested For recursive: the separator cascade, strongest first.
prefix_section gr_segment_spec() TRUE advanced untested For structural: prepend the heading.
semantic_window gr_segment_spec() 2 advanced untested For semantic: sentences embedded together.
semantic_percentile gr_segment_spec() 90 advanced untested For semantic: how extreme a distance counts as a boundary.
proposition_batch_tokens gr_segment_spec() 900 advanced untested For proposition: the size of each batch sent to the model.
parallel gr_segment_spec() NULL advanced untested Parallelise per-chunk model work.
context_reply_tokens gr_segment_spec() 90 advanced untested For contextual under llm: the output cap of each context-line request.
context_document_tokens gr_segment_spec() 1500 advanced untested For contextual under llm: how much of the document each request carries.
proposition_reply_tokens gr_segment_spec() 2000 advanced untested For proposition: the output cap of each batch’s request.
semantic_threshold gr_segment_spec() percentile advanced untested For semantic: how the distances between windows are cut into boundaries.
table_packing gr_segment_spec() rows advanced untested For paragraph: how the rows of a table are packed into chunks.
proposition_check gr_segment_spec() count advanced untested For proposition: whether a proposition with no support in its batch is dropped.
proposition_context_tokens gr_segment_spec() 0 advanced untested For proposition: tokens of the batch before that each batch’s request carries.
packing gr_segment_spec() greedy advanced untested How units are packed into chunks under the cap.
runt_merge gr_segment_spec() backward advanced untested Which way a chunk under min_tokens is merged.

Read

With these settings you choose how the model reads the chunks. The stage also holds the ones gr_read_many() adds for a folder. vignette("readers") covers them.

setting where default tier status description
on_overflow gr_read_spec() warn advanced untested For stuff: truncate with a warning, or stop, when the document does not fit.
context_order gr_read_spec() relevance advanced untested Where the selected chunks sit in the prompt.
restate gr_read_spec() auto advanced untested Whether to repeat the question before the excerpts as well as after.
premise gr_read_spec() FALSE advanced untested Check the question’s assumptions against the document.
verify gr_read_spec() FALSE basic untested Check the answer’s quotations against the chunks they cite.
effort gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested Reasoning effort, one level or a map named by call stem.
reader gr_read_spec() map_reduce basic untested The reading strategy.
model gr_read_spec() NULL basic untested Chat model id; NULL means the client’s.
temperature gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested Sampling temperature.
max_answer_tokens gr_read_spec() 1500 advanced untested Output cap for final answers and merges.
max_chunk_tokens gr_read_spec() 700 advanced untested Output cap for per-chunk calls.
max_summary_tokens gr_read_spec() 500 advanced untested Output cap for summarisation calls.
top_k gr_read_spec() 6 basic untested Chunks to use, for retrieve, rerank and iterative.
min_score gr_read_spec() -Inf advanced untested For retrieve: chunks scoring below this are dropped.
mmr gr_read_spec() 1 advanced untested Relevance against diversity when selecting chunks; 1 is plain top-k.
rerank_candidates gr_read_spec() 20 advanced untested For rerank: how many chunks to score.
rerank_min_score gr_read_spec() 4 advanced untested For rerank: the score below which a chunk is discarded.
fan_in gr_read_spec() 5 advanced untested For hierarchical: summaries combined per call.
max_levels gr_read_spec() 5 advanced untested For hierarchical: the recursion depth cap.
max_rounds gr_read_spec() 4 advanced untested For iterative: retrieve-assess cycles.
preview_tokens gr_read_spec() 1200 advanced untested For preview: the cap on the outline the planner sees.
members gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested For ensemble: the reader names to combine.
cite gr_read_spec() FALSE basic untested Ask for chunk-level citations in the answer.
skim_model gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested A cheaper model for skim’s extraction and rerank’s scoring.
summary_model gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested A cheaper model for hierarchical’s summaries.
parallel gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested Run per-chunk calls in parallel.
delay_between_calls gr_read_spec() 0 advanced untested Seconds to sleep between sequential calls.
accept_near_verbatim gr_read_spec() FALSE advanced untested Under verify, let a near-verbatim quotation stop the iterative reader.
max_merge_levels gr_read_spec() 6 advanced untested Most merge levels a reader runs before it returns its findings unmerged.
restate_tokens gr_read_spec() 1200 advanced untested Under restate = ‘auto’, the body length above which the question is repeated.
bm25_k1 gr_read_spec() 1.5 advanced cited BM25 term-frequency saturation, for rerank’s prefilter and lexical retrieve.
bm25_b gr_read_spec() 0.75 advanced cited BM25 length normalisation, for rerank’s prefilter and lexical retrieve.
lexical_blend gr_read_spec() 0.5 advanced untested For retrieve on lexical embeddings: the weight of cosine against BM25.
unskip_k gr_read_spec() 0 advanced untested For preview: the sections that best match the question’s words, read even when the plan skips them.
reread_on gr_read_spec() never advanced untested For preview: under “not_found”, an answer that found nothing reads the sections not read in full in one more request.
low_score gr_read_spec() not_found advanced untested For rerank: when every candidate scores below rerank_min_score, answer not found, or send the 5 best to the answer request.
fusion gr_read_spec() default advanced untested For retrieve and iterative: how embedding similarity and BM25 are combined into one ranking.
rrf_k gr_read_spec() 60 advanced cited Under fusion = ‘rrf’: the constant k in 1 / (k + rank).
answer_format gr_read_spec() parsed advanced untested How answering requests report their outcome: parsed from free text, or in a JSON schema the request forces.
premise_verdict gr_read_spec() sentence advanced untested Under premise = TRUE: the verdict as a sentence in the reply, or as schema fields with a quote that is checked against the excerpts.
context_policy gr_read_spec() NULL advanced untested Which pieces of a request are never cut, which are cut first, and which part of a cut piece is kept.
refine_state gr_read_spec() draft advanced untested For refine: carry a rewritten draft down the document, or a numbered list of findings that each request adds to, replaces or drops from.
effort_mode gr_read_spec() static advanced untested Under “escalate”, every stage starts at effort (“low” when unset), and the next stage is sent at “high” when a trigger fires.
recipe gr_read_many() thorough basic One recipe, applied to every document.
store gr_read_many() NULL basic Optional directory.
on_error gr_read_many() continue advanced “continue” (default) records the failure and moves on; “stop” aborts.
max_total_usd gr_read_many() NULL basic Stop once the run has spent this much, marking the remaining documents “skipped”, except any restored from store, which costs nothing.
max_total_calls gr_read_many() NULL advanced Stop before a document once the run has made this many requests, marking the rest “skipped”, except any restored from store, which makes no request.
keep_answers gr_read_many() TRUE advanced Keep every gr_answer in the result.
recursive gr_read_many() FALSE advanced Descend into subdirectories when sources is a directory.

Screening

The arguments of these functions, which vignette("review") covers:

  • gr_screen(), which decides which documents a review reads.
  • gr_reference() and gr_calibrate(), which measure the screening against a person.
  • gr_screen_sample_size() and gr_stop_test(), the sample size and stopping tests.
setting where default tier status description
recipe gr_screen() research basic The ingest and segmentation to use.
store gr_screen() NULL advanced Optional directory.
screen_tokens gr_screen() NULL basic untested Cap what the model is shown, in tokens, counted from the start of the document.
on_error gr_screen() continue advanced “continue” (default) records the failure and moves on; “stop” aborts.
max_total_usd gr_screen() NULL basic Stop once the run has spent this much, marking the remaining documents “skipped”, except any restored from store, which costs nothing.
max_total_calls gr_screen() NULL advanced Stop before a document once the run has made this many requests, marking the rest “skipped”, except any restored from store, which makes no request.
keep_answers gr_screen() FALSE advanced Keep the underlying gr_answer objects in $answers.
recursive gr_screen() FALSE advanced Descend into subdirectories when sources is a directory.
criteria_schema gr_screen() decision advanced untested What each screening reply holds.
samples gr_screen() 1 advanced untested How many times each document’s screening request is sent, from 1 to 20.
sample_rule gr_screen() include_if_any advanced untested How draws are combined when samples is above 1.
n gr_reference() 50 basic How many to draw: a whole number of at least 1.
of gr_reference() excluded basic Which rows to sample from: “excluded”, “kept” (include and unclear), “all”, or “stacked” (every kept record and a sample of the excluded ones).
seed gr_reference() NULL advanced A seed for the draw, so it is reproducible: the sample is drawn after set.seed(seed) and your session’s random number stream is put back afterwards.
blind gr_reference() TRUE advanced Leave the model’s decision and reason out of the file.
frame gr_reference() NULL advanced The same as of, under the name gr_screen_sample_size() uses.
reviewers gr_reference() 1 advanced How many people will judge each record.
positive gr_calibrate() include advanced Which human decision counts as eligible: “include” or “exclude”.
min_positives gr_calibrate() 10 advanced For an “all” sample: below this many eligible studies the sensitivity estimate is reported but marked inadequate.
of gr_calibrate() NULL advanced Which part of the screening run the reference was drawn from: “excluded”, “kept”, “all” or “stacked”; anything else is an error.
recall_target gr_calibrate() 0.95 basic untested The recall the screener should reach, strictly between 0 and 1.
conf gr_calibrate() 0.95 basic untested Confidence level of the recall and loss bounds.
max_lost gr_calibrate() NULL advanced Optional: the most eligible records the screener may have excluded.
max_width gr_calibrate() 0.1 advanced untested For a sample of one stratum: the widest interval, as a proportion, its headline rate may have for the sample to be adequate.
recall_target gr_screen_sample_size() 0.95 basic untested The recall to show, strictly between 0 and 1.
conf gr_screen_sample_size() 0.95 basic untested Confidence level of the one-sided bound.
prevalence gr_screen_sample_size() NULL basic Expected share of eligible records among those drawn, for frame = “all”: turns the eligible records needed into records to draw.
frame gr_screen_sample_size() all advanced “all”, “excluded” or “stacked”, as in gr_reference().
max_lost gr_screen_sample_size() NULL advanced For “excluded” and “stacked”: the most eligible records the screener may have excluded while still meeting the target.
frame_n gr_screen_sample_size() NULL advanced Number of records in the frame sampled: the excluded records for “excluded” and “stacked”, everything screened for “all”, where with prevalence it caps the draw at the whole frame.
target gr_stop_test() 0.95 basic Recall level, strictly between 0 and 1.
alpha gr_stop_test() 0.05 advanced Significance level, strictly between 0 and 1.
n_total gr_stop_test() NULL advanced Total number of records, screened or not.

Extraction

The arguments of gr_extract(). The recipe settings you pass to it in ... are the ingest and segment settings above.

setting where default tier status description
recipe gr_extract() research basic The ingest and segmentation to use.
store gr_extract() NULL advanced Optional directory.
resolve gr_extract() first basic untested What to do when two parts of one document give different values for the same field.
require_quote gr_extract() FALSE basic untested Discard any value that is not verified: one with no quote, a quote that is not verbatim in the chunk it cited, or a quote that does not state the value (see “Verifying it” below).
on_error gr_extract() continue advanced “continue” (default) records the failure and moves on; “stop” aborts.
max_total_usd gr_extract() NULL advanced Stop once the run has spent this much, marking the remaining documents “skipped”, except any restored from store, which costs nothing.
max_total_calls gr_extract() NULL advanced Stop before a document once the run has made this many requests, marking the rest “skipped”, except any restored from store, which makes no request.
keep_answers gr_extract() FALSE advanced Keep the underlying gr_answer objects in $answers.
recursive gr_extract() FALSE advanced Descend into subdirectories when sources is a directory.
agreement_columns gr_extract() FALSE advanced untested Add two columns per field to table, after the field columns: _agreement, how many of the chunks that reported the field give its most common value, of all that reported it (“2/3”), and _conflict, TRUE when they gave more than one value.

Synthesis

The arguments of gr_claims(), gr_outline(), gr_gaps() and gr_synthesise().

setting where default tier status description
model gr_claims() NULL basic Passed to the model call.
temperature gr_claims() NULL advanced Passed to the model call.
max_claim_tokens gr_claims() 1600 advanced Passed to the model call.
include_unclear gr_claims() FALSE advanced Keep rows with nothing extracted.
effort gr_claims() NULL advanced Reasoning effort, or NULL (the default) to send none: one string, or a character vector named by stage, as effort in gr_read_spec().
unverified gr_claims() exclude advanced untested What the claims prompt does with an extracted value whose quote did not verify, or that came with no quote (see gr_extract(), “Verifying it”).
model gr_outline() NULL advanced Passed to the model call.
temperature gr_outline() NULL advanced Passed to the model call.
max_sections gr_outline() 6 basic Upper bound on sections, before the closing one.
closing gr_outline() What is missing advanced The heading of the closing section, which receives gap claims and anything unplaced.
max_outline_tokens gr_outline() NULL advanced The reply limit for the outline call.
effort gr_outline() NULL advanced Reasoning effort, or NULL (the default) to send none: one string, or a character vector named by stage, as effort in gr_read_spec().
alternatives gr_outline() 1 advanced How many outlines to ask for, from 1 to 10.
max_cells gr_gaps() 40 advanced Cap on reported empty combinations, which grow as the product of two fields’ sizes.
min_reported gr_gaps() 0.5 advanced A field missing for more than this fraction of studies is reported as not reported.
model gr_synthesise() NULL basic Overrides for the writing calls.
max_section_tokens gr_synthesise() 1200 advanced Overrides for the writing calls.
temperature gr_synthesise() NULL advanced Overrides for the writing calls.
include_unclear gr_synthesise() FALSE advanced Write from rows whose extraction was incomplete.
cite_style gr_synthesise() auto basic How citations appear in the finished prose.
style gr_synthesise() NULL advanced A register instruction appended to the writing prompts, such as “formal academic; hedge claims; past tense for findings”.
coherence gr_synthesise() FALSE basic untested Revision passes over the finished draft: TRUE for all three, FALSE for none, or any of “structure” (reorder and merge), “cut” (remove repetition) and “register” (polish sentences) by name.
references gr_synthesise() TRUE advanced Append a ## References section built from the studies the finished text actually cites.
effort gr_synthesise() NULL advanced Reasoning effort, or NULL (the default) to send none: one string, or a character vector named by stage, as effort in gr_read_spec().
coherence_rounds gr_synthesise() 1 advanced untested How many rounds each coherence pass may run: each round revises the text the round before it kept, and the pass stops at the first round that is discarded or changes nothing.
figure_bands gr_synthesise() c(about = 0.1, over = 0.25, under = 0.25) advanced untested How near a value a qualified figure must be to count as found in the check of figures (see “Figures”): a named numeric vector of about (the share either way that “about 1,200” covers), over (the share above that “more than 1,000” covers) and under (the share below that “fewer than 1,000” covers).
prominence gr_synthesise() c(top = 1/3, middle = 1/3) advanced untested How much of the writing prompt’s sentence budget the claims of a section get, by rank: c(top = , middle = ), the shares of a section’s claims (ranked by the sign test of their direction tally, lowest p first, with a claim more of whose studies contradict it than support it last, then by the weight of the studies behind them; see gr_claims(), “Direction of effect”) asked for “two or three sentences” and “one or two sentences”; the rest get “one sentence”, and a section of three claims or fewer gives each “two or three”.
study_weights gr_synthesise() NULL advanced How much each study counts when claims are ranked, among claims whose sign tests tie (and so which tier each claim gets, see prominence): NULL (the default) for the package’s weight, 0.5 + 0.5 * size + 0.5 * filled, where size is log1p(n) over its largest value (the mean of the known ones when n is missing) and filled the share of a row’s filled cells whose quotations verified (0.5 when unknown).
revision_check gr_synthesise() lexicon advanced untested What checks a kept revision pass beyond the citation, figure and length checks.

Evaluation

The arguments of hr_benchmark(), hr_report(), hr_judge(), gr_compare(), hr_error_correlation() and hr_step_command(). vignette("evaluate") and vignette("compare") cover them.

setting where default tier status description

scorer hr_benchmark() hr_scorer_exact() basic An hr_scorer(); hr_scorer_exact() by default.
split hr_benchmark() test advanced The split or splits of the reference to run on.
governor hr_benchmark() NULL basic An hr_governor() the whole benchmark is held to, or NULL to take the limits from hr_options().
seed hr_benchmark() 1 advanced The seed of the arms’ private random stream.
contrasts hr_report() NULL advanced Pairs of arms to compare: a two-column character matrix of arm names, each row giving first minus second.
B hr_report() 2000 advanced Number of cluster bootstrap resamples, at least 100.
conf hr_report() 0.95 basic Confidence level of every interval.
k hr_report() c(1, 3, 5) advanced The values of k for pass^k.
seed hr_report() 1 advanced Seed of the private random stream the resamples are drawn from; the caller’s random state is left as it was.
method hr_report() auto basic “auto”, “bootstrap”, “cluster_t”, “bayes” or “exact”, as above.
confirmatory hr_report() FALSE advanced TRUE for a confirmatory report, which raises the default B to 5000 and refuses dev-split rows.
auto_bootstrap_at hr_report() c(items = 300, clusters = 30) advanced Under method = “auto”, the size at which the report switches from the cluster-robust t interval to the studentised cluster bootstrap: c(items = , clusters = ), both reached.
min_runs hr_report() 5 advanced The fewest runs for which the report gives intervals; below it the report is descriptive only.
mode hr_judge() select basic “select”, “grade” or “pairwise”.
model hr_judge() NULL basic The judge’s model; the client’s model when NULL.
orders hr_judge() 2 basic Presentation orders.
governor hr_judge() NULL advanced Optional hr_governor() for the judge’s requests.
draw_index hr_judge() 0 advanced Draw index passed to every request (see hr_call()).
recipes gr_compare() c("fast", "needle", "thorough") basic A character vector of recipe names, or a list of gr_recipes.
allow_duplicates gr_compare() FALSE advanced Run duplicates anyway (useful at temperature > 0 to measure variance).
on_error gr_compare() continue advanced “continue” keeps going and records the failure; “stop” aborts the whole comparison.
strata hr_error_correlation() NULL advanced untested NULL to stratify by difficulty, or each item’s stratum: a vector named by item, or one value per item in the order of unique(bench$item).
n_strata hr_error_correlation() 3 advanced untested How many difficulty strata, when strata is NULL: a whole number from 1 to 10, default 3.

held_out hr_error_correlation() TRUE advanced untested TRUE (the default) reads only the rows that count as evidence (reportable, so not the dev split); FALSE reads every row.
seed hr_error_correlation() 1 advanced untested The seed of the private random stream the sample is drawn with; the caller’s random state is left as it was.
parse hr_step_command() exit basic untested How the result is read: “exit” or “testthat”.
timeout hr_step_command() 60 advanced untested Seconds the program may run before it is stopped, from 1 to 86400.
held hr_step_command() FALSE advanced untested Whether the result is kept from the steps after this one and left for the scorer.

Options

Session settings. You set them with hr_options(), and a run reads them when it starts. vignette("runs") covers the limits.

setting where default tier status description
verbose hr_options() TRUE basic Print a line for each ingest, segment and read stage.
tokenizer hr_options() heuristic advanced Token counter: “heuristic” (conservative, no dependencies), “words”, “chars”, “tiktoken” (needs reticulate), or a name registered via hr_set_tokenizer().
model hr_options() gpt-5.6-terra basic Default chat model.
embedding_model hr_options() text-embedding-3-small advanced Default embedding model.
api_base hr_options() https://api.openai.com/v1 advanced API root; point this at a proxy or a compatible endpoint.
api_headers hr_options() character(0) advanced Named character vector of extra HTTP headers sent with every request, for gateways that do not authenticate with a bearer token.
api hr_options() responses advanced “responses” or “chat” request shape.
temperature hr_options() NULL advanced untested Default sampling temperature.
max_retries hr_options() 4 advanced untested Retries for transient failures.
retry_pause_base hr_options() 2 advanced untested Seconds; exponential backoff base.
request_timeout hr_options() 120 advanced untested Per-request timeout, seconds.
safety_margin hr_options() 0.1 advanced untested Fraction of the context window left unused to absorb tokenizer error.
min_output_tokens hr_options() 256 advanced untested Floor on the completion room hr_budget() reserves when reserve_output is not given explicitly.
cache_documents hr_options() TRUE advanced Cache ingestion per file + settings.
cache_embeddings hr_options() TRUE advanced Cache embeddings per text + model.
cache_dir hr_options() NULL basic Directory hr_cache() stores model responses in.
embedder hr_options() NULL advanced Which registered embedder to use.
parallel hr_options() FALSE advanced Run per-chunk calls concurrently.
workers hr_options() 4 advanced untested Worker processes when parallel is TRUE.
max_cost_usd hr_options() 5 basic Spending limit per run, in USD.
max_calls hr_options() 400 basic Hard cap on model calls per run, checked before every request.
max_tokens_total hr_options() NULL advanced Most tokens one run may use: the prompt and reply tokens of every call, cache hits included, and the text sent to be embedded.
max_output_tokens hr_options() NULL advanced The largest output cap one request may be sent with.
allowed_models hr_options() NULL advanced Character vector of the model ids a run may call, chat and embedding models alike.
allow_unpriced hr_options() FALSE advanced Whether a chat model with no registered price may be called while max_cost_usd is set.
unknown_model_action hr_options() warn advanced “warn” or “error” when a model id is not in the registry.
actor hr_options() list() advanced A named list (or character vector) of the actor fields every hr_trace() records: system, owner, run_by, purpose and approved_by, each one string.
auto_max_tokens hr_options() 50000 advanced untested The largest document, in tokens, that answer_document() with recipe = “auto” reads with “fast” (one request); a larger one is read with “thorough”.
auto_room_share hr_options() 0.5 advanced untested The second condition of that choice: the document must fill at most this share of the input room hr_budget() leaves on every model of the run.
reasoning_floor hr_options() 2048 advanced untested The smallest output cap a request to a reasoning model is sent with.
output_reserve_share hr_options() 0.25 advanced untested The share of the usable window hr_budget() reserves for the reply when no reserve_output is given, between min_output_tokens and the model’s output limit.
near_verbatim_sim hr_options() 0.9 advanced measured The least similarity a quotation of at least near_verbatim_short_chars characters (after normalising), and one shorter than that, needs for the edit-distance matcher to score it near_verbatim (see gr_verify_evidence()).
near_verbatim_sim_short hr_options() 0.95 advanced measured The least similarity a quotation of at least near_verbatim_short_chars characters (after normalising), and one shorter than that, needs for the edit-distance matcher to score it near_verbatim (see gr_verify_evidence()).
near_verbatim_short_chars hr_options() 40 advanced measured The least similarity a quotation of at least near_verbatim_short_chars characters (after normalising), and one shorter than that, needs for the edit-distance matcher to score it near_verbatim (see gr_verify_evidence()).

Building blocks

Some settings choose a module from a registry: extractor, clean, method, reader, hr_options(embedder = ), and the recipe you give answer_document(). The tables below show the registries as installed, so a module you register with gr_register_reader() or another gr_register_*() function (vignette("extending")) appears in them too.

Extractors

An extractor turns one kind of file into text. harnessr picks it by the file’s extension unless you name one with extractor.

knitr::kable(gr_extractors()[, c("name", "extensions", "needs", "description")])
name extensions needs description
txt txt txt, text, log, csv, tsv Plain text, including delimited files
md md md, markdown, rmd, qmd Markdown, keeping heading structure
html html html, htm, xhtml xml2 HTML via xml2, keeping heading structure
pdf pdf pdf pdftools PDF with per-page OCR fallback and page provenance
docx docx docx, dotx xml2 Word: headings, tables by row, footnotes and endnotes; OCRs embedded images
image image png, jpg, jpeg, tif, tiff, bmp, gif tesseract Image OCR

Cleaners and presets

A cleaner removes one kind of noise from the text. Cleaners marked default_on run unless the preset or list you give leaves them out. early cleaners run before late ones, whatever order you name them in.

knitr::kable(gr_cleaners()[, c("name", "stage", "default_on", "description")])
name stage default_on description
captions early FALSE Drop figure/table caption lines: ‘Table 2.’, ‘Figure 3:’, ‘Fig. 3 |’, ‘Table 2 Baseline …’ or the label alone, not ‘Table 2 shows …’ (OFF by default: a caption can be the only statement of a result)
emails early FALSE Remove email addresses
headers_footers early FALSE Drop running heads and feet: short lines repeated at the top or bottom of many pages, or at the edge of blocks where pages are not known
hyphenation early TRUE Rejoin words split across line breaks by PDF layout (‘mito-’, ‘LIA-’ in capitals); a compound the document writes with its hyphen elsewhere (‘follow-up’) keeps it; number ranges (‘18-’) and compounds (‘Anglo-’) are left alone
page_numbers early TRUE Drop decorated page-number lines (‘Page 4’, ‘- 12 -’, ‘[12]’, and ‘12.’ unless the line before runs on into it); bare numbers are kept
references early FALSE Drop a trailing bibliography, from a References/Bibliography heading to the end; in a Markdown file a line indented 4 or more spaces is code, not a heading
urls early FALSE Remove URLs (OFF by default: URLs are often the answer)
ascii_only late FALSE Transliterate to ASCII (drops accents and non-Latin scripts)
collapse_whitespace late TRUE Collapse runs of spaces/tabs and 2+ consecutive blank lines, and trim block edges; preserves paragraph breaks
control_chars late TRUE Strip control and zero-width characters that survive PDF extraction
ligatures late TRUE Expand typographic ligatures and straighten smart quotes; en and em dashes are kept
lowercase late FALSE Lowercase everything (loses proper-noun and acronym signal)
remove_numbers late FALSE Replace every digit with a space. OFF by default: this makes figures, dates and percentages unanswerable
remove_punctuation late FALSE Replace punctuation with spaces. OFF by default: destroys sentence boundaries

A preset is a named list of cleaners. This table shows the steps each preset runs, read from what it did to the example report:

presets <- c("none", "minimal", "standard", "academic", "scan", "legacy")
knitr::kable(data.frame(preset = presets, cleaners = vapply(presets, function(p) {
  steps <- names(gr_ingest(gr_example(), gr_ingest_spec(clean = p))$stats$clean_log)
  if (length(steps)) paste(steps, collapse = ", ") else "(none)"
}, character(1)), row.names = NULL))
preset cleaners
none (none)
minimal control_chars, collapse_whitespace
standard page_numbers, hyphenation, control_chars, ligatures, collapse_whitespace
academic page_numbers, captions, references, hyphenation, control_chars, ligatures, collapse_whitespace
scan page_numbers, headers_footers, hyphenation, control_chars, ligatures, collapse_whitespace
legacy page_numbers, captions, urls, emails, references, remove_numbers, collapse_whitespace

Segmenters

A segmenter decides where chunks are cut. cost says what it spends: free, embedding for one embedding pass, or llm for model requests.

knitr::kable(gr_segmenters()[, c("name", "cost", "needs_client", "description")])
name cost needs_client description
contextual free FALSE Paragraph chunks prefixed with where they sit; context_source=‘llm’ writes it per chunk, one request each (calls_max = chunks).
fixed free FALSE Uniform token windows, ignoring structure. The control condition.
page free FALSE One chunk per page. For forms, invoices and scanned records.
paragraph free FALSE Greedy packing of the author’s paragraphs up to the cap.
proposition llm TRUE Rewrite into standalone factual statements. Expensive; best for dense factual recall.
recursive free FALSE Cascade through separators, using the strongest one that fits.
semantic embedding TRUE Cut where consecutive embeddings diverge most. One embedding pass.
sentence free FALSE Sentence-boundary packing; tighter, more chunks, cleaner edges.
structural free FALSE Never merge across headings; each chunk keeps its section title.

Readers

A reader decides how the chunks reach the model. signature records which chunks it sends, how many requests it makes, and how information passes between them. cost_calls is the number of requests.

knitr::kable(gr_readers()[, c("name", "signature", "cost_calls", "description")])
name signature cost_calls description
ensemble ensemble|sum+1|none sum of members + 1 Run several distinct readers and adjudicate. Members must have different signatures.
extract all|N+conflicts|none N (+1 per conflict with resolve = ‘model’) Fill a typed schema from every chunk, then reconcile. Needs fields.
hierarchical all|N+tree+1|tree N + fan-in levels + 1 Recursively summarise until the summaries fit, then answer. Truly recursive.
iterative topk|rounds*2|forward up to 2 x max_rounds Agentic loop: the model names what it still needs and that drives the next retrieval.
map_reduce all|N+logN|tree N + merges Answer each chunk independently, then tree-reduce. Parallel, order-independent.
preview planned|1+s+1|none 1 + skimmed sections + 1 Plan from an outline first, then read only what the plan says to. Sections it skips are named.
refine all|N|forward N Sequential draft-and-revise down the document. Order matters; not parallelisable.
rerank topk|m+1|none m + 1 BM25 prefilter, then the model scores candidates, then answer from the winners.
retrieve topk|1|none 1 + embeddings Embed, rank by cosine similarity, answer from the top k. Cost independent of length.
screen head|1|none 1 Decide whether one document meets a review’s criteria, from its opening. Needs include/exclude.
skim all|N+1|none N + 1 Extract verbatim evidence per chunk, then answer once from the evidence.
stuff all|1|none 1 Whole document in one prompt. The baseline; errors or truncates if it does not fit.

Embedders

An embedder turns text into vectors for the retrieve and iterative readers and the semantic segmenter. A deterministic embedder gives the same vectors every run, which a replay needs.

knitr::kable(gr_embedders()[, c("name", "deterministic", "description")])
name deterministic description
api FALSE Embeddings endpoint on the client’s base URL
lexical TRUE Hashed bag-of-words; free, offline, word overlap not meaning

Recipes

A recipe names an ingestion, a segmentation and a reader, with their settings. The table shows the values each built-in recipe sets, and you can override any of them by name.

knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(gr_recipes()), function(n) {
  r <- gr_recipes(n)
  data.frame(recipe = n, clean = paste(r$ingest$clean, collapse = ", "),
             method = r$segment$method, max_tokens = r$segment$max_tokens,
             overlap_tokens = r$segment$overlap_tokens, reader = r$read$reader,
             top_k = r$read$top_k)
})))
recipe clean method max_tokens overlap_tokens reader top_k
fast standard paragraph 4000 0 stuff 6
precise standard sentence 600 60 skim 6
needle standard semantic 500 50 retrieve 8
thorough standard paragraph 1200 120 map_reduce 6
survey standard structural 1500 0 hierarchical 6
narrative standard paragraph 1500 0 refine 6
scanned scan page 2000 0 rerank 6
research academic structural 900 90 iterative 5
consensus standard recursive 1000 100 ensemble 6
legacy legacy paragraph 3000 0 map_reduce 6
